**Them There** is a [theatrical production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_production "Theatrical production")[collective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective "Collective") made up of a group of [comedy writers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy "Comedy") and performers, notable for working on a range of projects together including the first five series of _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_. They are also informally referred to as the **_Horrible Histories_ troupe**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-WhatsOnTV-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-DigitalSpy_01-2) and _**The Six Idiots**_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-5)

## Collective

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Collective")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/250px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

The group at the 2011 Children's BAFTAs

The collective is made up of [Mathew Baynton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton "Mathew Baynton"), [Simon Farnaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby "Simon Farnaby"), [Martha Howe-Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas "Martha Howe-Douglas"), [Jim Howick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick "Jim Howick"), [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), and [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond"). All members contribute writing and acting to their productions.

The group initially collaborated for the children's TV show _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, but have continued to collaborate since then.

They formed the formal Them There identity for the start of the production of _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-6) and the collective is credited for the [production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_producer "Television producer") alongside [Monumental Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_Studios "ITV Studios").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-8)

## Works

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Works")]

### _Horrible Histories_ (2009–2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Horrible Histories (2009–2013)")]

Main article: [Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(2009_TV_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")

_**Horrible Histories**_ was a British [sketch comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sketch_comedy "Sketch comedy") and [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_film "Musical film") television series, based on the [children's history books of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(book_series) "Horrible Histories (book series)"). The show was produced for [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC") by [Lion Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All3Media "All3Media") with Citrus Television and ran from 2009 to 2013 for five series of thirteen half-hour episodes, with additional one-off seasonal and Olympic specials. The creative team was largely recruited from the UK comedy scene, including the central troupe alongside a large supporting cast headed by [Katy Wix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Wix "Katy Wix"), [Lawry Lewin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawry_Lewin "Lawry Lewin"), [Alice Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Lowe "Alice Lowe") and [Dominique Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Moore "Dominique Moore"). As well as carrying over the graphic style and much of the content of the [_Horrible Histories_ book series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(book_series) "Horrible Histories (book series)"), the approach and humour of the show was inspired by past British historical comedies, including _[Blackadder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackadder "Blackadder")_ and the [Monty Python](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monty_Python "Monty Python") films.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-telegraph_a-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-radiotimes-10)

Each episode covered multiple eras in history, named for their respective book titles. The show combined [live-action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live-action "Live-action") sketches, which often [parody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody "Parody") other UK media or celebrities, with [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"), [animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animation "Animation") and [quizzes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quiz "Quiz"). The series was a critical and ratings success, winning numerous domestic and international awards. In 2011 the show was the subject of a [Live Prom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_Prom "Horrible Histories Prom") at the [Royal Albert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall"), where sketches and songs from the series were performed live. The cast left the series in 2014,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-BCGS6-11) with the [series continuing with a new creative team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(2015_TV_series) "Horrible Histories (2015 TV series)") the next year.

### _Yonderland_ (2013–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Yonderland (2013–2016)")]

Main article: [Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")

Following the end of _Horrible Histories_, the troupe reunited for _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a [sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") that was broadcast on [Sky 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_1 "Sky 1") from November 2013 to December 2016. Howe-Douglas starred as 33-year-old Debbie Maddox, who becomes increasingly bored with her life as a suburban [stay-at-home mother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stay-at-home_mother "Stay-at-home mother") until an elf (Baynton) appears from a portal in her cupboard, insisting that she's the "chosen one" destined to save the eponymous fantasy world. Reluctantly, Debbie agrees to meet with the Elders of the realm... only to discover that they've lost the scroll that explains what the chosen one is supposed to do. As it turns out, Yonderland is a silly, magical place, threatened by the evil Negatus (Farnaby). It will take all of Debbie's resources to complete each week's quest in time to pick up her children from school.

### _Bill_ (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Bill (2015)")]

Main article: [Bill (2015 film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_(2015_film) "Bill (2015 film)")

The group's first film, _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, was released on 18 September 2015. Whilst not officially related to the _Horrible Histories_ series, it was produced by the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), reunited and starred the original core performers of the series, and shared the comedic approach of its historical content.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-BBCMediaCentre_03-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-Comedy_co_uk_01-13)

### _Ghosts_ (2019–2023)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Ghosts (2019–2023)")]

Main article: [Ghosts (2019 TV series)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts_(2019_TV_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")

_**Ghosts**_ is the troupe's most recent series, which they co-created, write and star in. It is a [sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") which was broadcast on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") from 2019 to 2023 over five series. It centres on a group of ghosts from different historical periods haunting a [country house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_house "Country house") they share with its new living occupants (played by [Kiell Smith-Bynoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiell_Smith-Bynoe "Kiell Smith-Bynoe") and [Charlotte Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Ritchie "Charlotte Ritchie")).

The six members of the Them There troupe play seven of the nine principal ghost characters (with [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard") playing both caveman 'Robin' and the head of headless Sir Humphrey Bone), alongside two additional ghosts played by [Katy Wix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Wix "Katy Wix") and [Lolly Adefope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lolly_Adefope "Lolly Adefope"), who, along with Smith-Bynoe, both also appeared alongside the core team on Horrible Histories.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-mediacentre2-14) They also each play a ghost from the [plague pit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plague_pit "Plague pit").

All members of the collective have writing credits for different episodes, with every episode written by one or two of the cast. Baynton wrote the most episodes, having (co-)written 16 of the 34 episodes, mostly with Howick (15 episodes). Rickard has written 14 episodes, Willbond 9, Howe-Douglas 6, and Farnaby 2.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-15)

The series was the first [post-watershed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-watershed "Post-watershed") comedy by the ensemble, although some television critics noted that the series was suitable for adults and children alike,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-times-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-eveningstandard-17) and it was moved to a pre-watershed slot from series 2 onwards. Reviews of the series have been positive, with critics appreciating the high joke rate, the premise and the strength of the acting ensemble. The series was made by the production company Monumental Pictures, part of [ITV Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_Studios "ITV Studios").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-mediacentre2-14) It is filmed [on location](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Location_shooting "Location shooting") at [West Horsley Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Horsley_Place "West Horsley Place") in [Surrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrey "Surrey").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-telegraph-18) The show ran for five series, with four Christmas specials,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-BBCMediaCentre-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-comedy.co.uk_2022-11-24-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-comedy.co.uk_2022-09-07-21) and one [Comic Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Relief "Comic Relief") special featuring [Kylie Minogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylie_Minogue "Kylie Minogue").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-23)

The show was [remade for an American audience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts_(American_TV_series) "Ghosts (American TV series)"), starring [Rose McIver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_McIver "Rose McIver") and [Utkarsh Ambudkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utkarsh_Ambudkar "Utkarsh Ambudkar"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-hollywoodreporter.com-24) and Mathew Baynton from the UK cast has had a guest [cameo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance "Cameo appearance") on the US version.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-25)

### _Ghosts: The Possession of Button House_ (2026)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House (2026)")]

Main article: [Ghosts: The Possession of Button House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts:_The_Possession_of_Button_House "Ghosts: The Possession of Button House")

The group announced the film _Ghosts: The Possession of Button House_ through social media (primarily Instagram) on 27 February 2026, with filming set to begin in early March 2026. It is based on the original BBC1 television series, and is being filmed with Monumental Pictures. It will be released by [Lionsgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_UK "Lionsgate UK") in the UK and Ireland on 23 October 2026.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-27)

**Them There** is a [theatrical production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theatrical_production "Theatrical production")[collective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective "Collective") made up of a group of [comedy writers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy "Comedy") and performers, notable for working on a range of projects together including the first five series of _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_. They are also informally referred to as the **_Horrible Histories_ troupe**[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-WhatsOnTV-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-DigitalSpy_01-2) and _**The Six Idiots**_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-5)

## Collective

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Collective")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/250px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

The group at the 2011 Children's BAFTAs

The collective is made up of [Mathew Baynton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton "Mathew Baynton"), [Simon Farnaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby "Simon Farnaby"), [Martha Howe-Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas "Martha Howe-Douglas"), [Jim Howick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick "Jim Howick"), [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), and [Ben Willbond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond "Ben Willbond"). All members contribute writing and acting to their productions.

The group initially collaborated for the children's TV show _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, but have continued to collaborate since then.

They formed the formal Them There identity for the start of the production of _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-6) and the collective is credited for the [production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_producer "Television producer") alongside [Monumental Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_Studios "ITV Studios").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-8)

## Works

### _Horrible Histories_ (2009–2013)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Horrible Histories (2009–2013)")]

Main article: [Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(2009_TV_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")

_**Horrible Histories**_ was a British [sketch comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sketch_comedy "Sketch comedy") and [musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musical_film "Musical film") television series, based on the [children's history books of the same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(book_series) "Horrible Histories (book series)"). The show was produced for [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC") by [Lion Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All3Media "All3Media") with Citrus Television and ran from 2009 to 2013 for five series of thirteen half-hour episodes, with additional one-off seasonal and Olympic specials. The creative team was largely recruited from the UK comedy scene, including the central troupe alongside a large supporting cast headed by [Katy Wix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Wix "Katy Wix"), [Lawry Lewin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lawry_Lewin "Lawry Lewin"), [Alice Lowe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Lowe "Alice Lowe") and [Dominique Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dominique_Moore "Dominique Moore"). As well as carrying over the graphic style and much of the content of the [_Horrible Histories_ book series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(book_series) "Horrible Histories (book series)"), the approach and humour of the show was inspired by past British historical comedies, including _[Blackadder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blackadder "Blackadder")_ and the [Monty Python](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monty_Python "Monty Python") films.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-telegraph_a-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-radiotimes-10)

Each episode covered multiple eras in history, named for their respective book titles. The show combined [live-action](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live-action "Live-action") sketches, which often [parody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parody "Parody") other UK media or celebrities, with [music videos](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video"), [animations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animation "Animation") and [quizzes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quiz "Quiz"). The series was a critical and ratings success, winning numerous domestic and international awards. In 2011 the show was the subject of a [Live Prom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_Prom "Horrible Histories Prom") at the [Royal Albert Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Albert_Hall "Royal Albert Hall"), where sketches and songs from the series were performed live. The cast left the series in 2014,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-BCGS6-11) with the [series continuing with a new creative team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(2015_TV_series) "Horrible Histories (2015 TV series)") the next year.

### _Yonderland_ (2013–2016)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Yonderland (2013–2016)")]

Main article: [Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")

Following the end of _Horrible Histories_, the troupe reunited for _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a [sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") that was broadcast on [Sky 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_1 "Sky 1") from November 2013 to December 2016. Howe-Douglas starred as 33-year-old Debbie Maddox, who becomes increasingly bored with her life as a suburban [stay-at-home mother](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stay-at-home_mother "Stay-at-home mother") until an elf (Baynton) appears from a portal in her cupboard, insisting that she's the "chosen one" destined to save the eponymous fantasy world. Reluctantly, Debbie agrees to meet with the Elders of the realm... only to discover that they've lost the scroll that explains what the chosen one is supposed to do. As it turns out, Yonderland is a silly, magical place, threatened by the evil Negatus (Farnaby). It will take all of Debbie's resources to complete each week's quest in time to pick up her children from school.

### _Bill_ (2015)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Bill (2015)")]

Main article: [Bill (2015 film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_(2015_film) "Bill (2015 film)")

The group's first film, _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, was released on 18 September 2015. Whilst not officially related to the _Horrible Histories_ series, it was produced by the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC"), reunited and starred the original core performers of the series, and shared the comedic approach of its historical content.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-BBCMediaCentre_03-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-Comedy_co_uk_01-13)

### _Ghosts_ (2019–2023)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Ghosts (2019–2023)")]

Main article: [Ghosts (2019 TV series)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts_(2019_TV_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")

_**Ghosts**_ is the troupe's most recent series, which they co-created, write and star in. It is a [sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") which was broadcast on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") from 2019 to 2023 over five series. It centres on a group of ghosts from different historical periods haunting a [country house](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_house "Country house") they share with its new living occupants (played by [Kiell Smith-Bynoe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kiell_Smith-Bynoe "Kiell Smith-Bynoe") and [Charlotte Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Ritchie "Charlotte Ritchie")).

The six members of the Them There troupe play seven of the nine principal ghost characters (with [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard") playing both caveman 'Robin' and the head of headless Sir Humphrey Bone), alongside two additional ghosts played by [Katy Wix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Wix "Katy Wix") and [Lolly Adefope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lolly_Adefope "Lolly Adefope"), who, along with Smith-Bynoe, both also appeared alongside the core team on Horrible Histories.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-mediacentre2-14) They also each play a ghost from the [plague pit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plague_pit "Plague pit").

All members of the collective have writing credits for different episodes, with every episode written by one or two of the cast. Baynton wrote the most episodes, having (co-)written 16 of the 34 episodes, mostly with Howick (15 episodes). Rickard has written 14 episodes, Willbond 9, Howe-Douglas 6, and Farnaby 2.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-15)

The series was the first [post-watershed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-watershed "Post-watershed") comedy by the ensemble, although some television critics noted that the series was suitable for adults and children alike,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-times-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-eveningstandard-17) and it was moved to a pre-watershed slot from series 2 onwards. Reviews of the series have been positive, with critics appreciating the high joke rate, the premise and the strength of the acting ensemble. The series was made by the production company Monumental Pictures, part of [ITV Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_Studios "ITV Studios").[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-mediacentre2-14) It is filmed [on location](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Location_shooting "Location shooting") at [West Horsley Place](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Horsley_Place "West Horsley Place") in [Surrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surrey "Surrey").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-telegraph-18) The show ran for five series, with four Christmas specials,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-BBCMediaCentre-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-comedy.co.uk_2022-11-24-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-comedy.co.uk_2022-09-07-21) and one [Comic Relief](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comic_Relief "Comic Relief") special featuring [Kylie Minogue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kylie_Minogue "Kylie Minogue").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-23)

The show was [remade for an American audience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts_(American_TV_series) "Ghosts (American TV series)"), starring [Rose McIver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_McIver "Rose McIver") and [Utkarsh Ambudkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utkarsh_Ambudkar "Utkarsh Ambudkar"),[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-hollywoodreporter.com-24) and Mathew Baynton from the UK cast has had a guest [cameo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cameo_appearance "Cameo appearance") on the US version.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-25)

### _Ghosts: The Possession of Button House_ (2026)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Them_There&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Ghosts: The Possession of Button House (2026)")]

Main article: [Ghosts: The Possession of Button House](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts:_The_Possession_of_Button_House "Ghosts: The Possession of Button House")

The group announced the film _Ghosts: The Possession of Button House_ through social media (primarily Instagram) on 27 February 2026, with filming set to begin in early March 2026. It is based on the original BBC1 television series, and is being filmed with Monumental Pictures. It will be released by [Lionsgate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionsgate_UK "Lionsgate UK") in the UK and Ireland on 23 October 2026.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them_There#cite_note-27)

**Ben Willbond** is an English actor and screenwriter best known as a member of the British Them There collective, for which he has written and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.

Along with fellow Them There member [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), he co-wrote the 2015 feature film _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_ and 2022 feature-length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ben_Willbond&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Willbond was a [Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Armed_Forces "British Armed Forces") child and consequently his family moved around every two years. He was sent to [board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boarding_school "Boarding school") at [Stamford School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_School "Stamford School") in [Lincolnshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincolnshire "Lincolnshire"), when he was nine years old. He was bullied whilst attending the school.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-2) Willbond, when talking about his experience at the school, said "I don't actually remember that time because it was so shocking".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-3) He studied Russian and French at [St Catherine's College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Catherine's_College,_Oxford "St Catherine's College, Oxford").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ben_Willbond&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Along with Arnold Widdowson, Willbond was part of the comedy duo "Ben & Arn", who won the [Perrier Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perrier_Award "Perrier Award") for "Best Newcomer" in 1999,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) and formed the self-proclaimed "thinking man's [French pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_pop_music "French pop music") duo"[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-5) Priorité à Gauche.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-Guardian20050817-6) He then went on to perform his solo character shows at several [Edinburgh Fringe Festivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Fringe_Festival "Edinburgh Fringe Festival"), the last being in 2005 which also starred [Katy Brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Brand "Katy Brand") and [Jim Field Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Field_Smith "Jim Field Smith").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-Guardian20050817-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-7)

He is perhaps best known for his regular role in [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in which he played a wide variety of historical figures, most memorably recurring roles as [Henry VIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_VIII "Henry VIII") and [Alexander the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great "Alexander the Great"). Along with the five other members of the _Horrible Histories_ starring cast, Willbond is also the co-creator, -writer and -star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family [fantasy comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_comedy "Fantasy comedy") series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-8) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare"), which involved the same starring troupe.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-9)

Previously, Willbond had starred in a short-lived [sketch show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sketch_comedy "Sketch comedy") for [ITV2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV2 "ITV2") called _Laura, Ben & Him_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) with [Marek Larwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marek_Larwood "Marek Larwood") and sometime writing partner [Laura Solon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Solon "Laura Solon"). He also appeared in Solon's [BBC Radio 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_4 "BBC Radio 4") sketch show, _[Laura Solon: Talking and Not Talking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura\_Solon:\_Talking\_and\_Not\_Talking "Laura Solon: Talking and Not Talking")_. Other notable television work includes the recurring roles of Steve Warwick in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") comedy _[Rev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rev.\_(TV\_series) "Rev. (TV series)")_,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-BBCRevS2E4-10) Adam Kenyon in [BBC Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Four "BBC Four")'s _[The Thick of It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Thick\_of\_It "The Thick of It")_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) and as a television director in the movie-length final episode of the [Ricky Gervais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Gervais "Ricky Gervais") comedy _[Extras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extras\_(TV\_series) "Extras (TV series)")_ ([BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Two "BBC Two")).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) He has also appeared in _[Katy Brand's Big Ass Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy\_Brand's\_Big\_Ass\_Show "Katy Brand's Big Ass Show")_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) for [ITV2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV2 "ITV2") and _[Mayo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayo\_(TV\_series) "Mayo (TV series)")_[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-AvalonCV-11) for [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One").

Willbond's other radio credits include [BBC Radio 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_4 "BBC Radio 4") series _[Deep Trouble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep\_Trouble\_(radio\_comedy\_series) "Deep Trouble (radio comedy series)")_, _[Double Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double\_Science "Double Science")_ (co-written with [Justin Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Edwards_(actor) "Justin Edwards (actor)")), _Recorded for Training Purposes_ and the first series of _[Electric Ink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric\_Ink "Electric Ink")_. He also starred in the YouTube [romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy")_Nigel and Victoria_.

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/91/Philips_Casting_f%C3%BCr_Youtube-Web-Soap_%22Nigel_and_Victoria%22_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Philips_Casting_f%C3%BCr_Youtube-Web-Soap_%22Nigel_and_Victoria%22_(cropped).jpg)

Willbond in 2011

His 2010 short film _[Tooty's Wedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooty's\_Wedding "Tooty's Wedding")_, which he co-wrote with Solon, won numerous international comedy awards and was screened as part of the [2012 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Sundance_Film_Festival "2012 Sundance Film Festival").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-Huffington_20111215-12) Other notable film work includes the movie _[Starter for 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starter\_for\_10\_(film) "Starter for 10 (film)")_ (2006).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-13) In 2007 he had a short appearance in _[St Trinian's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St\_Trinian's\_(film) "St Trinian's (film)")_,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-AvalonCV-11) as a nervous school inspector.

Between 2019 and 2023, Willbond portrayed The Captain in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_ with the other main _Horrible Histories_ cast.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ben_Willbond&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Willbond has two children and is married to Charlotte Gordon. He is a keen [cricketer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") and plays for the Thunderers.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-14)

**Ben Willbond** is an English actor and screenwriter best known as a member of the British Them There collective, for which he has written and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.

Along with fellow Them There member [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), he co-wrote the 2015 feature film _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_ and 2022 feature-length television comedy [_We Are Not Alone_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_Not_Alone_(2022_film) "We Are Not Alone (2022 film)").

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ben_Willbond&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Willbond was a [Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Armed_Forces "British Armed Forces") child and consequently his family moved around every two years. He was sent to [board](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boarding_school "Boarding school") at [Stamford School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamford_School "Stamford School") in [Lincolnshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincolnshire "Lincolnshire"), when he was nine years old. He was bullied whilst attending the school.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-2) Willbond, when talking about his experience at the school, said "I don't actually remember that time because it was so shocking".[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-3) He studied Russian and French at [St Catherine's College, Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St_Catherine's_College,_Oxford "St Catherine's College, Oxford").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ben_Willbond&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Along with Arnold Widdowson, Willbond was part of the comedy duo "Ben & Arn", who won the [Perrier Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perrier_Award "Perrier Award") for "Best Newcomer" in 1999,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) and formed the self-proclaimed "thinking man's [French pop](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/French_pop_music "French pop music") duo"[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-5) Priorité à Gauche.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-Guardian20050817-6) He then went on to perform his solo character shows at several [Edinburgh Fringe Festivals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Fringe_Festival "Edinburgh Fringe Festival"), the last being in 2005 which also starred [Katy Brand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy_Brand "Katy Brand") and [Jim Field Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Field_Smith "Jim Field Smith").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-Guardian20050817-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-7)

He is perhaps best known for his regular role in [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, in which he played a wide variety of historical figures, most memorably recurring roles as [Henry VIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_VIII "Henry VIII") and [Alexander the Great](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_the_Great "Alexander the Great"). Along with the five other members of the _Horrible Histories_ starring cast, Willbond is also the co-creator, -writer and -star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family [fantasy comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fantasy_comedy "Fantasy comedy") series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-8) In addition he is the co-writer of _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare"), which involved the same starring troupe.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-9)

Previously, Willbond had starred in a short-lived [sketch show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sketch_comedy "Sketch comedy") for [ITV2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV2 "ITV2") called _Laura, Ben & Him_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) with [Marek Larwood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marek_Larwood "Marek Larwood") and sometime writing partner [Laura Solon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura_Solon "Laura Solon"). He also appeared in Solon's [BBC Radio 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_4 "BBC Radio 4") sketch show, _[Laura Solon: Talking and Not Talking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laura\_Solon:\_Talking\_and\_Not\_Talking "Laura Solon: Talking and Not Talking")_. Other notable television work includes the recurring roles of Steve Warwick in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") comedy _[Rev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rev.\_(TV\_series) "Rev. (TV series)")_,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-BBCRevS2E4-10) Adam Kenyon in [BBC Four](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Four "BBC Four")'s _[The Thick of It](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Thick\_of\_It "The Thick of It")_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) and as a television director in the movie-length final episode of the [Ricky Gervais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Gervais "Ricky Gervais") comedy _[Extras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extras\_(TV\_series) "Extras (TV series)")_ ([BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Two "BBC Two")).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) He has also appeared in _[Katy Brand's Big Ass Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katy\_Brand's\_Big\_Ass\_Show "Katy Brand's Big Ass Show")_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-feca2011-4) for [ITV2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV2 "ITV2") and _[Mayo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayo\_(TV\_series) "Mayo (TV series)")_[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-AvalonCV-11) for [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One").

Willbond's other radio credits include [BBC Radio 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Radio_4 "BBC Radio 4") series _[Deep Trouble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep\_Trouble\_(radio\_comedy\_series) "Deep Trouble (radio comedy series)")_, _[Double Science](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double\_Science "Double Science")_ (co-written with [Justin Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Justin_Edwards_(actor) "Justin Edwards (actor)")), _Recorded for Training Purposes_ and the first series of _[Electric Ink](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric\_Ink "Electric Ink")_. He also starred in the YouTube [romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy")_Nigel and Victoria_.

[![Image 5](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/9/91/Philips_Casting_f%C3%BCr_Youtube-Web-Soap_%22Nigel_and_Victoria%22_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail_unscaled)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Philips_Casting_f%C3%BCr_Youtube-Web-Soap_%22Nigel_and_Victoria%22_(cropped).jpg)

Willbond in 2011

His 2010 short film _[Tooty's Wedding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooty's\_Wedding "Tooty's Wedding")_, which he co-wrote with Solon, won numerous international comedy awards and was screened as part of the [2012 Sundance Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Sundance_Film_Festival "2012 Sundance Film Festival").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-Huffington_20111215-12) Other notable film work includes the movie _[Starter for 10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starter\_for\_10\_(film) "Starter for 10 (film)")_ (2006).[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-13) In 2007 he had a short appearance in _[St Trinian's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St\_Trinian's\_(film) "St Trinian's (film)")_,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-AvalonCV-11) as a nervous school inspector.

Between 2019 and 2023, Willbond portrayed The Captain in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_ with the other main _Horrible Histories_ cast.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ben_Willbond&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Willbond has two children and is married to Charlotte Gordon. He is a keen [cricketer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") and plays for the Thunderers.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Willbond#cite_note-14)

**Mathew John Baynton** is an English actor, comedian, musician and writer. He is a member of the Them There[collective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective "Collective"), in which he wrote and starred in _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. He was also the co-creator, writer and star of the [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama")_[The Wrong Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wrong\_Mans "The Wrong Mans")_. Other television roles include Elliot Ward in _[A Good Girl's Guide to Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Good\_Girl's\_Guide\_to\_Murder\_(TV\_series) "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder (TV series)")_, Deano in _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_, Chris Pitt-Goddard in _[Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spy\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Spy (2011 TV series)")_, Simon in _[Peep Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peep\_Show\_(British\_TV\_series) "Peep Show (British TV series)")_, William Agar in _[Quacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quacks\_(TV\_series) "Quacks (TV series)")_, and twin brothers Jamie Winton and Ariel Conroy in _[You, Me and the Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You,\_Me\_and\_the\_Apocalypse "You, Me and the Apocalypse")_. He has appeared in several films, including _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_ (2015) and _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_ (2023).

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mathew_Baynton&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Mathew Baynton grew up in [Southend-on-Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southend-on-Sea "Southend-on-Sea"), Essex.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-theprotagonistmagazine_mathew-baynton-1)He is the youngest of three boys, with two older brothers, Daniel and Andrew.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-cc-2)

He was educated at [Southend High School for Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southend_High_School_for_Boys "Southend High School for Boys"). He graduated with [first class honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_class_honours "First class honours") from the [Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Bruford_College_of_Speech_and_Drama "Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-cc-2) and later trained in [clowning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clown "Clown") at [École Philippe Gaulier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Gaulier "Philippe Gaulier") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-3)

Baynton's second cousins [Daisy May Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daisy_May_Cooper "Daisy May Cooper") and [Charlie Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Cooper_(actor) "Charlie Cooper (actor)") are also in the acting profession.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-4)[Trevor Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Cooper "Trevor Cooper") is his first cousin once removed.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mathew_Baynton&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Acting and writing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mathew_Baynton&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Acting and writing")]

Baynton is one of the performers of the children's television series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, appearing in the first five series as an actor, singer, and occasional writer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-TelWest-6) Baynton and the other five members of the main _Horrible Histories_ cast form the Them There troupe, which has since created other shows.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/500px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

L-R: [Simon Farnaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby "Simon Farnaby"), [Martha Howe-Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas "Martha Howe-Douglas"), Mathew Baynton, [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), Ben Willbond and [Jim Howick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick "Jim Howick") at the 2011 Children's [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTAs "BAFTAs").

Along with the other members of the troupe, Baynton is the creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family fantasy comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-7) He starred with the same troupe in _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")[family comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") film based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare"), who ventures to [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") to pursue his dream of becoming a [playwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playwright "Playwright").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-9) The troupe also reunited in 2019 to create the BBC series _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, with Baynton appearing as a [Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanticism "Romanticism") poet named Thomas Thorne.

Baynton teamed with friend and fellow _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_ alumnus [James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Corden "James Corden") to create, write, and star in _[The Wrong Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wrong\_Mans "The Wrong Mans")_, a [comedy thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_thriller "Comedy thriller") for [BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Two "BBC Two") that premiered in autumn 2013.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-10) The series is co-produced by online television provider [Hulu.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu.com "Hulu.com") in the United States, where it premiered in November 2013.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-11) The first six-part series proved a critical and commercial success, and a similarly well-received two-part sequel was broadcast in December 2014.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-12)

Other notable TV comedy roles include Deano in _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_; Chris in the [Darren Boyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Boyd "Darren Boyd") sitcom vehicle _[Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spy\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Spy (2011 TV series)")_; and William in the 2017 [black comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_comedy "Black comedy") series _[Quacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quacks\_(TV\_series) "Quacks (TV series)")_.

In 2009, he appeared in a [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for [Mercury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Prize "Mercury Prize")-nominated band [The Bees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bees_(English_band) "The Bees (English band)").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-13)

Baynton appeared at the 2013 [Edinburgh Fringe Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Fringe_Festival "Edinburgh Fringe Festival"), starring in the world premiere of [Tom Basden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Basden "Tom Basden")'s play _Holes_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-14) He reprised his role of Gus in a London revival of the same play in summer 2014.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-15)

In late 2015, Baynton portrayed Jamie Winton and his brother Ariel Conroy in [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One")'s [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction "Science fiction")[comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") miniseries _[You, Me and the Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You,\_Me\_and\_the\_Apocalypse "You, Me and the Apocalypse")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In January 2024, Baynton made his [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") debut in [Eleanor Rhode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleanor_Rhode "Eleanor Rhode")'s production of _[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Midsummer\_Night's\_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")_ as [Nick Bottom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Bottom "Nick Bottom") at the [Royal Shakespeare Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Theatre "Royal Shakespeare Theatre"), [Stratford-upon-Avon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratford-upon-Avon "Stratford-upon-Avon"), before transferring to the [Barbican Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbican_Centre "Barbican Centre") in December 2024.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-17)

In January 2025, it was announced that Baynton would appear as a contestant on the nineteenth series of the [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4") show _[Taskmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taskmaster\_(TV\_series) "Taskmaster (TV series)")_ alongside [Fatiha El-Ghorri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatiha_El-Ghorri "Fatiha El-Ghorri"), [Jason Mantzoukas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Mantzoukas "Jason Mantzoukas"), [Rosie Ramsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_Ramsey "Rosie Ramsey"), and [Stevie Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Martin "Stevie Martin").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-18) Baynton would go on to win the series. Bayton also participated in _[Taskmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taskmaster\_(TV\_series) "Taskmaster (TV series)") Champion of Champions 4,_ which aired in December 2025. He won, beating [Andy Zaltzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Zaltzman "Andy Zaltzman"), [Maisie Adam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maisie_Adam "Maisie Adam"), [Sam Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Campbell_(comedian) "Sam Campbell (comedian)") and [John Robins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Robins_(comedian) "John Robins (comedian)").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-19)

Baynton is a former member of the band Special Benny as a vocalist and guitarist.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-20) Their debut album _Toys_ was released in 2010.

He has also performed as a solo act under the name Dog Ears. His debut solo EP, _So It Goes_, was released in November 2011.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-21) It consists of four self-penned songs.

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mathew_Baynton&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Baynton and his partner Kelly Robinson, a [film historian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_film "History of film"), have two children. Baynton and Robinson had a [civil partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_union "Civil union") ceremony in 2023.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-22)

Baynton said in a 2013 interview that he would be happy for his son to become an actor, if he enjoyed acting.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-:0-23) He tries to keep his children out of the spotlight; however, he raised awareness about breaking [gender stereotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_role "Gender role") after his son was mocked for wearing a pink bicycle helmet.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-:1-24)

**Mathew John Baynton** is an English actor, comedian, musician and writer. He is a member of the Them There[collective](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collective "Collective"), in which he wrote and starred in _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. He was also the co-creator, writer and star of the [comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_drama "Comedy drama")_[The Wrong Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wrong\_Mans "The Wrong Mans")_. Other television roles include Elliot Ward in _[A Good Girl's Guide to Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Good\_Girl's\_Guide\_to\_Murder\_(TV\_series) "A Good Girl's Guide to Murder (TV series)")_, Deano in _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_, Chris Pitt-Goddard in _[Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spy\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Spy (2011 TV series)")_, Simon in _[Peep Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peep\_Show\_(British\_TV\_series) "Peep Show (British TV series)")_, William Agar in _[Quacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quacks\_(TV\_series) "Quacks (TV series)")_, and twin brothers Jamie Winton and Ariel Conroy in _[You, Me and the Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You,\_Me\_and\_the\_Apocalypse "You, Me and the Apocalypse")_. He has appeared in several films, including _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_ (2015) and _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_ (2023).

## Early life and education

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mathew_Baynton&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")]

Mathew Baynton grew up in [Southend-on-Sea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southend-on-Sea "Southend-on-Sea"), Essex.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-theprotagonistmagazine_mathew-baynton-1)He is the youngest of three boys, with two older brothers, Daniel and Andrew.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-cc-2)

He was educated at [Southend High School for Boys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southend_High_School_for_Boys "Southend High School for Boys"). He graduated with [first class honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_class_honours "First class honours") from the [Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rose_Bruford_College_of_Speech_and_Drama "Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-cc-2) and later trained in [clowning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clown "Clown") at [École Philippe Gaulier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Gaulier "Philippe Gaulier") in [Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris "Paris").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-3)

Baynton's second cousins [Daisy May Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daisy_May_Cooper "Daisy May Cooper") and [Charlie Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie_Cooper_(actor) "Charlie Cooper (actor)") are also in the acting profession.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-4)[Trevor Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Cooper "Trevor Cooper") is his first cousin once removed.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mathew_Baynton&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Acting and writing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mathew_Baynton&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Acting and writing")]

Baynton is one of the performers of the children's television series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, appearing in the first five series as an actor, singer, and occasional writer.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-TelWest-6) Baynton and the other five members of the main _Horrible Histories_ cast form the Them There troupe, which has since created other shows.

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/500px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

L-R: [Simon Farnaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby "Simon Farnaby"), [Martha Howe-Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas "Martha Howe-Douglas"), Mathew Baynton, [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), Ben Willbond and [Jim Howick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick "Jim Howick") at the 2011 Children's [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTAs "BAFTAs").

Along with the other members of the troupe, Baynton is the creator, writer, and star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, a family fantasy comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-7) He starred with the same troupe in _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC")[family comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sitcom "Sitcom") film based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare"), who ventures to [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") to pursue his dream of becoming a [playwright](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Playwright "Playwright").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-9) The troupe also reunited in 2019 to create the BBC series _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, with Baynton appearing as a [Romantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romanticism "Romanticism") poet named Thomas Thorne.

Baynton teamed with friend and fellow _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_ alumnus [James Corden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Corden "James Corden") to create, write, and star in _[The Wrong Mans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Wrong\_Mans "The Wrong Mans")_, a [comedy thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy_thriller "Comedy thriller") for [BBC Two](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_Two "BBC Two") that premiered in autumn 2013.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-10) The series is co-produced by online television provider [Hulu.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hulu.com "Hulu.com") in the United States, where it premiered in November 2013.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-11) The first six-part series proved a critical and commercial success, and a similarly well-received two-part sequel was broadcast in December 2014.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-12)

Other notable TV comedy roles include Deano in _[Gavin & Stacey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gavin\_&\_Stacey "Gavin & Stacey")_; Chris in the [Darren Boyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Boyd "Darren Boyd") sitcom vehicle _[Spy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spy\_(2011\_TV\_series) "Spy (2011 TV series)")_; and William in the 2017 [black comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_comedy "Black comedy") series _[Quacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quacks\_(TV\_series) "Quacks (TV series)")_.

In 2009, he appeared in a [music video](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") for [Mercury Prize](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_Prize "Mercury Prize")-nominated band [The Bees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bees_(English_band) "The Bees (English band)").[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-13)

Baynton appeared at the 2013 [Edinburgh Fringe Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh_Fringe_Festival "Edinburgh Fringe Festival"), starring in the world premiere of [Tom Basden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Basden "Tom Basden")'s play _Holes_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-14) He reprised his role of Gus in a London revival of the same play in summer 2014.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-15)

In late 2015, Baynton portrayed Jamie Winton and his brother Ariel Conroy in [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One")'s [science fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Science_fiction "Science fiction")[comedy-drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comedy-drama "Comedy-drama") miniseries _[You, Me and the Apocalypse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/You,\_Me\_and\_the\_Apocalypse "You, Me and the Apocalypse")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In January 2024, Baynton made his [Royal Shakespeare Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Company "Royal Shakespeare Company") debut in [Eleanor Rhode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleanor_Rhode "Eleanor Rhode")'s production of _[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Midsummer\_Night's\_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")_ as [Nick Bottom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nick_Bottom "Nick Bottom") at the [Royal Shakespeare Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_Shakespeare_Theatre "Royal Shakespeare Theatre"), [Stratford-upon-Avon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratford-upon-Avon "Stratford-upon-Avon"), before transferring to the [Barbican Centre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbican_Centre "Barbican Centre") in December 2024.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-17)

In January 2025, it was announced that Baynton would appear as a contestant on the nineteenth series of the [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4") show _[Taskmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taskmaster\_(TV\_series) "Taskmaster (TV series)")_ alongside [Fatiha El-Ghorri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatiha_El-Ghorri "Fatiha El-Ghorri"), [Jason Mantzoukas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Mantzoukas "Jason Mantzoukas"), [Rosie Ramsey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosie_Ramsey "Rosie Ramsey"), and [Stevie Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stevie_Martin "Stevie Martin").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-18) Baynton would go on to win the series. Bayton also participated in _[Taskmaster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taskmaster\_(TV\_series) "Taskmaster (TV series)") Champion of Champions 4,_ which aired in December 2025. He won, beating [Andy Zaltzman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_Zaltzman "Andy Zaltzman"), [Maisie Adam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maisie_Adam "Maisie Adam"), [Sam Campbell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Campbell_(comedian) "Sam Campbell (comedian)") and [John Robins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Robins_(comedian) "John Robins (comedian)").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-19)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mathew_Baynton&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Baynton and his partner Kelly Robinson, a [film historian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_film "History of film"), have two children. Baynton and Robinson had a [civil partnership](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Civil_union "Civil union") ceremony in 2023.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-22)

Baynton said in a 2013 interview that he would be happy for his son to become an actor, if he enjoyed acting.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-:0-23) He tries to keep his children out of the spotlight; however, he raised awareness about breaking [gender stereotypes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gender_role "Gender role") after his son was mocked for wearing a pink bicycle helmet.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathew_Baynton#cite_note-:1-24)

**James Howick** (born 14 May 1979) is an English actor and writer, known for his appearances in television series such as _[Peep Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peep\_Show\_(British\_TV\_series) "Peep Show (British TV series)")_ (2007–2012), _[Sex Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex\_Education\_(TV\_series) "Sex Education (TV series)")_ (2019–2022), and _[Here We Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here\_We\_Go\_(TV\_series) "Here We Go (TV series)")_ (2022–present). Howick is additionally associated with the creative collective Them There, with whom he has written and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ (2009–2013), _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ (2013–2016), and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019–2023).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jim_Howick&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

James Howick was born in [Chichester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chichester "Chichester"), [West Sussex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Sussex "West Sussex") on 14 May 1979, but grew up in [Bognor Regis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bognor_Regis "Bognor Regis").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-Guardian-3) He was educated at [The Regis School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Regis_School "The Regis School").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-4) He graduated with [First Class Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Class_Honours "First Class Honours") from [Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountview_Academy_of_Theatre_Arts "Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts") in 2000.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jim_Howick&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, which includes Ben Willbond, [Martha Howe-Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas "Martha Howe-Douglas"), Mathew Baynton, [Simon Farnaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby "Simon Farnaby") and [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), Howick is also the co-creator, -writer and -star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, an eight-part family fantasy comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-6) He co-starred with the same troupe in _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-7) Other prominent television roles include Gerard in [_Peep Show_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peep_Show_(British_TV_series) "Peep Show (British TV series)"), Gerry in Danny Boyle's _[Babylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babylon\_(TV\_series) "Babylon (TV series)")_ and Anthony in the revival of _[Reggie Perrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie\_Perrin "Reggie Perrin")_. In addition he has been a regular guest star in various sketch comedies, including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_ and _[The Kevin Bishop Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kevin\_Bishop\_Show "The Kevin Bishop Show")_. In 2017, he played Aaron Mayford in the [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_channel) "ITV (TV channel)")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)")_[Broadchurch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadchurch "Broadchurch")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-8) From 2019 to 2023, Howick featured in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") original series [_Sex Education_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_Education_(TV_series) "Sex Education (TV series)") as Mr Hendricks, a science teacher at Moordale Secondary School who also conducts the Swing Band. Howick is the co-creator, co-writer and co-star of the BBC One sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, - Howick plays numerous characters, but is mostly known for his role as Patrick Butcher, a 1980s Scout Master who was killed in an archery accident - the show was first broadcast in 2019 and ran for five series. More recently, Howick was cast in the 2022 BBC comedy series _[Here We Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here\_We\_Go\_(TV\_series) "Here We Go (TV series)")_ in which he plays Paul Jessop.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-Guardian-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-9)

In film, Howick played Cpl. Matlin in the 2004 [Guillermo del Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_del_Toro "Guillermo del Toro") adaptation of _[Hellboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellboy\_(2004\_film) "Hellboy (2004 film)")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-Guardian-3)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jim_Howick&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Howick met his wife, Lauren, on the set of _[Reggie Perrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie\_Perrin "Reggie Perrin")_. They married in 2012 and live in [East Finchley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Finchley "East Finchley"), London.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-Guardian-3)

Howick is an avid _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ fan.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-10)

## Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jim_Howick&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Awards")]

In 2010, Howick won a Children's [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA") for his performance in the second series of the [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC_(TV_channel) "CBBC (TV channel)") television series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-14) In 2026, he was nominated for the [British Academy Television Award for Best Male Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_Best_Male_Comedy_Performance "British Academy Television Award for Best Male Comedy Performance") for _[Here We Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here\_We\_Go\_(TV\_series) "Here We Go (TV series)")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-15)
