**James Howick** (born 14 May 1979) is an English actor and writer, known for his appearances in television series such as _[Peep Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peep\_Show\_(British\_TV\_series) "Peep Show (British TV series)")_ (2007–2012), _[Sex Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex\_Education\_(TV\_series) "Sex Education (TV series)")_ (2019–2022), and _[Here We Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here\_We\_Go\_(TV\_series) "Here We Go (TV series)")_ (2022–present). Howick is additionally associated with the creative collective Them There, with whom he has written and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ (2009–2013), _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ (2013–2016), and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_ (2019–2023).

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jim_Howick&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

James Howick was born in [Chichester](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chichester "Chichester"), [West Sussex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Sussex "West Sussex") on 14 May 1979, but grew up in [Bognor Regis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bognor_Regis "Bognor Regis").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-Guardian-3) He was educated at [The Regis School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Regis_School "The Regis School").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-4) He graduated with [First Class Honours](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Class_Honours "First Class Honours") from [Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountview_Academy_of_Theatre_Arts "Mountview Academy of Theatre Arts") in 2000.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jim_Howick&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Along with the five other members of the _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_ starring cast, which includes Ben Willbond, [Martha Howe-Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas "Martha Howe-Douglas"), Mathew Baynton, [Simon Farnaby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby "Simon Farnaby") and [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), Howick is also the co-creator, -writer and -star of _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, an eight-part family fantasy comedy series that premiered on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") on 10 November 2013.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-6) He co-starred with the same troupe in _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, a BBC-produced comedy film based loosely around the early life of William Shakespeare.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-7) Other prominent television roles include Gerard in [_Peep Show_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peep_Show_(British_TV_series) "Peep Show (British TV series)"), Gerry in Danny Boyle's _[Babylon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babylon\_(TV\_series) "Babylon (TV series)")_ and Anthony in the revival of _[Reggie Perrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie\_Perrin "Reggie Perrin")_. In addition he has been a regular guest star in various sketch comedies, including _[The Armstrong and Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Armstrong\_and\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong and Miller Show")_ and _[The Kevin Bishop Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Kevin\_Bishop\_Show "The Kevin Bishop Show")_. In 2017, he played Aaron Mayford in the [ITV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ITV_(TV_channel) "ITV (TV channel)")[thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thriller_(genre) "Thriller (genre)")_[Broadchurch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Broadchurch "Broadchurch")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-8) From 2019 to 2023, Howick featured in the [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") original series [_Sex Education_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_Education_(TV_series) "Sex Education (TV series)") as Mr Hendricks, a science teacher at Moordale Secondary School who also conducts the Swing Band. Howick is the co-creator, co-writer and co-star of the BBC One sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, - Howick plays numerous characters, but is mostly known for his role as Patrick Butcher, a 1980s Scout Master who was killed in an archery accident - the show was first broadcast in 2019 and ran for five series. More recently, Howick was cast in the 2022 BBC comedy series _[Here We Go](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Here\_We\_Go\_(TV\_series) "Here We Go (TV series)")_ in which he plays Paul Jessop.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-Guardian-3)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-9)

In film, Howick played Cpl. Matlin in the 2004 [Guillermo del Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_del_Toro "Guillermo del Toro") adaptation of _[Hellboy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellboy\_(2004\_film) "Hellboy (2004 film)")_.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-Guardian-3)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Jim_Howick&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Howick met his wife, Lauren, on the set of _[Reggie Perrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reggie\_Perrin "Reggie Perrin")_. They married in 2012 and live in [East Finchley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Finchley "East Finchley"), London.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-Guardian-3)

Howick is an avid _[Star Wars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star\_Wars "Star Wars")_ fan.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Howick#cite_note-10)

'''Mathew John Baynton''' is an English actor, comedian, musician and writer. He is a member of the [[Them There]][[collective]], in which he wrote and starred in ''[[Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)|Horrible Histories]]'', ''[[Yonderland]]'' and ''[[Ghosts (2019 TV series)|Ghosts]]''. He was also the co-creator, writer and star of the [[Comedy drama|comedy-drama]]''[[The Wrong Mans]]''. Other television roles include Elliot Ward in ''[[A Good Girl's Guide to Murder (TV series)|A Good Girl's Guide to Murder]]'', Deano in ''[[Gavin & Stacey]]'', Chris Pitt-Goddard in ''[[Spy (2011 TV series)|Spy]]'', Simon in ''[[Peep Show (British TV series)|Peep Show]]'', William Agar in ''[[Quacks (TV series)|Quacks]]'', and twin brothers Jamie Winton and Ariel Conroy in ''[[You, Me and the Apocalypse]]''. He has appeared in several films, including ''[[Bill (2015 film)|Bill]]'' (2015) and ''[[Wonka (film)|Wonka]]'' (2023).

  

==Early life and education ==

Mathew Baynton grew up in [[Southend-on-Sea]], Essex.<ref name="theprotagonistmagazine_mathew-baynton"/>He is the youngest of three boys, with two older brothers, Daniel and Andrew.<ref name =cc/>

  

He was educated at [[Southend High School for Boys]]. He graduated with [[first class honours]] from the [[Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama]],<ref name =cc>{{cite web |url=http://www.calmccrystal.com/index.php?feature_id=33|title=Cal McCrystal}}</ref> and later trained in [[clown]]ing at [[Philippe Gaulier|École Philippe Gaulier]] in [[Paris]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://metro.co.uk/2013/11/20/matthew-baynton-we-couldnt-have-asked-for-the-wrong-mans-to-go-any-better-4192397/|title=Mathew Baynton: We couldn't have asked for The Wrong Mans to go any better |date=20 November 2013|work=Metro|access-date=20 November 2013}}</ref>

[[Trevor Cooper]] (first cousin once removed) | website = }} '''Mathew John Baynton''' is an English actor, comedian, musician and writer. He is a member of the [[Them There]][[collective]], in which he wrote and starred in ''[[Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)|Horrible Histories]]'', ''[[Yonderland]]'' and ''[[Ghosts (2019 TV series)|Ghosts]]''. He was also the co-creator, writer and star of the [[Comedy drama|comedy-drama]]''[[The Wrong Mans]]''. Other television roles include Elliot Ward in ''[[A Good Girl's Guide to Murder (TV series)|A Good Girl's Guide to Murder]]'', Deano in ''[[Gavin & Stacey]]'', Chris Pitt-Goddard in ''[[Spy (2011 TV series)|Spy]]'', Simon in ''[[Peep Show (British TV series)|Peep Show]]'', William Agar in ''[[Quacks (TV series)|Quacks]]'', and twin brothers Jamie Winton and Ariel Conroy in ''[[You, Me and the Apocalypse]]''. He has appeared in several films, including ''[[Bill (2015 film)|Bill]]'' (2015) and ''[[Wonka (film)|Wonka]]'' (2023). ==Early life and education == Mathew Baynton grew up in [[Southend-on-Sea]], Essex.He is the youngest of three boys, with two older brothers, Daniel and Andrew. He was educated at [[Southend High School for Boys]]. He graduated with [[first class honours]] from the [[Rose Bruford College of Speech and Drama]],{{cite web |url=http://www.calmccrystal.com/index.php?feature_id=33|title=Cal McCrystal}} and later trained in [[clown]]ing at [[Philippe Gaulier|École Philippe Gaulier]] in [[Paris]].{{cite news |url=https://metro.co.uk/2013/11/20/matthew-baynton-we-couldnt-have-asked-for-the-wrong-mans-to-go-any-better-4192397/|title=Mathew Baynton: We couldn't have asked for The Wrong Mans to go any better |date=20 November 2013|work=Metro|access-date=20 November 2013}} –—°′″≈≠≤≥±−×÷←→·§**Cite your sources:** [Edit summary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Edit_summary "Help:Edit summary")(Briefly describe your changes) By publishing changes, you agree to the [Terms of Use](https://foundation.wikimedia.org/wiki/Special:MyLanguage/Policy:Terms_of_Use "foundation:Special:MyLanguage/Policy:Terms of Use"), and you irrevocably agree to release your contribution under the [CC BY-SA 4.0 License](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_the_Creative_Commons_Attribution-ShareAlike_4.0_International_License "Wikipedia:Text of the Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License") and the [GFDL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Text_of_the_GNU_Free_Documentation_License "Wikipedia:Text of the GNU Free Documentation License"). **Simon Farnaby** (born 2 April 1973) is an English actor, comedian, writer and singer. He is best known for his work with the Them There collective where he has written and starred in productions including the sketch show [_Horrible Histories_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(2009_TV_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)"), _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and [_Ghosts_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts_(2019_British_TV_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)"), as well as writing for film.

Farnaby earned [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA") nominations for his writing of _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_, both for [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") and [Best British Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Film "BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-1) and was the winner of the 2023 [Television BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2) In 2023, he co-wrote and appeared in _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_, a film which serves as a prequel to the [Roald Dahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roald_Dahl "Roald Dahl") novel _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory")_, exploring [Willy Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willy_Wonka "Willy Wonka")'s origins.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Farnaby was born on 2 April 1973 in [Darlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darlington "Darlington"), [County Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Durham "County Durham")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-3) and attended [Richmond School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond_School "Richmond School"), [North Yorkshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Yorkshire "North Yorkshire").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Television work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Television work")]

Farnaby was a long-time member of _[The Mighty Boosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mighty\_Boosh "The Mighty Boosh")_ supporting cast,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-metro-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-ie-5) having had roles both in their series and co-starring in the quasi-spinoff film _[Bunny and the Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunny\_and\_the\_Bull "Bunny and the Bull")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-bunny-6)

Other notable television work includes recurring roles in the sitcoms _[Jam & Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jam\_&\_Jerusalem "Jam & Jerusalem")_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)_[The Midnight Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Midnight\_Beast\_(TV\_series) "The Midnight Beast (TV series)")_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-metro-4) and _[Detectorists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detectorists "Detectorists")_. He previously had a very brief role in one episode of _[Coronation Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation\_Street "Coronation Street")_ in the 1990s.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)

Farnaby has presented a number of factual programmes including _Richard III: The King in the Car Park_ in 2013,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-8) tracing the [discovery and identification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhumation_of_Richard_III_of_England "Exhumation of Richard III of England") of the remains of the last [Plantagenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantagenet "Plantagenet") king, the 2014 Channel 4 documentary series entitled _Man Vs Weird_, in which he travelled the world investigating people who claim superhuman abilities,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-9) and as narrator of the [Channel 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_5_(UK) "Channel 5 (UK)") docu-series called _[On the Yorkshire Buses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On\_the\_Yorkshire\_Buses "On the Yorkshire Buses")_, following [East Yorkshire Motor Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Yorkshire_Motor_Services "East Yorkshire Motor Services").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-10)

Farnaby accepted a [TV BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") in 2023 for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment"), for a short film broadcast as part of the [Platinum Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Party_at_the_Palace "Platinum Party at the Palace") for the [Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II") of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in June 2022, in which Farnaby played a butler.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2)

#### Them There

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Them There")]

Main article: Them There

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/250px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

L-R: Simon Farnaby, [Martha Howe-Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas "Martha Howe-Douglas"), Mathew Baynton, [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), Ben Willbond and Jim Howick at the 2011 Children's [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTAs "BAFTAs").

Farnaby has worked extensively with the Them There collective of six writers and actors, who started as principal members of the cast of the [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC") live-action series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, where he played offbeat characters including [Caligula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caligula "Caligula") and Death.

Farnaby, along with the five other collective members, co-created, wrote and starred in _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ (2013–2016),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-11) which was broadcast on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") for three series.

Farnaby had his first major involvement with the creation of a film with the troupe, on the 2015 historical comedy film _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-13)

The same collective then went on to create the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") show _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_, which ran for five seasons before the team decided to retire it.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-14) Farnaby played the fictitious [Conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") politician ghost, Julian Fawcett,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-15) who always appeared without trousers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)

### Books

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Books")]

Along with journalist Scott Murray, in 2011 Farnaby co-wrote _[The Phantom of the Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Open "The Phantom of the Open")_, a biography of [Maurice Flitcroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Flitcroft "Maurice Flitcroft"), a would-be professional golfer whose unsuccessful attempts to qualify for the [Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Championship "Open Championship") led to his being described as "the world's worst golfer".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-chortle-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-17)

His first children's novel, _The Wizard In My Shed_, was published in 2020,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-18) and this was followed by a sequel titled _Warrior in my Wardrobe: More Misadventures with Merdyn the Wild_, which was released in 2021.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-20)

Farnaby was also a co-author of _Ghosts: The Button House Archives_, a companion book to the Them There television series for the BBC, _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_ which he co-wrote and starred in.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-22)

### Films

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Films")]

Having previously appeared in _[The Mighty Boosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mighty\_Boosh "The Mighty Boosh")_, Farnaby was in a starring role for the related film _[Bunny and the Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunny\_and\_the\_Bull "Bunny and the Bull")_ in 2009, where he played the eponymous Bunny.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-bunny-6)

In 2016, Farnaby co-wrote and had a small acting part in _[Mindhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindhorn "Mindhorn")_ with [Julian Barratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Barratt "Julian Barratt"), a comedy about Richard Thorncroft (Barratt), a faded television actor drawn into negotiations with a criminal who believes his character Detective Mindhorn is real.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-ie-5)

He co-wrote the book _The Phantom of the Open_ about golfer [Maurice Flitcroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Flitcroft "Maurice Flitcroft") in 2011, and then started work on a film script of the story in 2017, which led to the release of _[The Phantom of the Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Open "The Phantom of the Open")_ in 2021, starring [Mark Rylance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Rylance "Mark Rylance").

Also in 2016, Farnaby had a small on-screen role in _[Rogue One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue\_One "Rogue One")_, as an X-Wing pilot.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-23)

The biggest film success of Farnaby's career came with the [Paddington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington_(film) "Paddington (film)") film franchise. Following on from appearing as an actor in [the first film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington_(film) "Paddington (film)"), he went on to co-write _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_ with [Paul King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_King_(director) "Paul King (director)"), for which he was nominated for two [film BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards") for [best adapted screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") and [Outstanding British Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Film "BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film"). He was also the winner of the International Online Cinema Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, and the [Hollywood Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Critics_Association "Hollywood Critics Association") award for Best Adapted Screenplay in 2018.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-24) Farnaby subsequently appeared alongside [Paddington Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington_Bear "Paddington Bear") and [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in a short film broadcast as a part of the [Platinum Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Party_at_the_Palace "Platinum Party at the Palace") for the [Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II") of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in June 2022, which won the 2023 [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment"), which Farnaby accepted.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2)

Farnaby is the co-writer of 2023 Christmas release _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_, along with [Paul King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_King_(director) "Paul King (director)"), which is a prequel to _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory")_ by [Roald Dahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roald_Dahl "Roald Dahl").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-25) Alongside _Ghosts_ co-star [Charlotte Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Ritchie "Charlotte Ritchie"), Farnaby also has a small on-screen role, with his Them There collaborator Mathew Baynton in one of the leading roles, and starring [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9e_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet").

Farnaby wrote the screenplay for [The Magic Faraway Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Magic_Faraway_Tree_(film) "The Magic Faraway Tree (film)").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-26) An adaptation of [Enid Blyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enid_Blyton "Enid Blyton")'s book series of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Faraway_Tree "The Faraway Tree"). The film released theatrically in the UK on 27 March 2026.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-27)

**Simon Farnaby** (born 2 April 1973) is an English actor, comedian, writer and singer. He is best known for his work with the Them There collective where he has written and starred in productions including the sketch show [_Horrible Histories_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible_Histories_(2009_TV_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)"), _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and [_Ghosts_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts_(2019_British_TV_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)"), as well as writing for film.

Farnaby earned [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA "BAFTA") nominations for his writing of _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_, both for [Best Adapted Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") and [Best British Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Film "BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-1) and was the winner of the 2023 [Television BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2) In 2023, he co-wrote and appeared in _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_, a film which serves as a prequel to the [Roald Dahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roald_Dahl "Roald Dahl") novel _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory")_, exploring [Willy Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Willy_Wonka "Willy Wonka")'s origins.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Farnaby was born on 2 April 1973 in [Darlington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darlington "Darlington"), [County Durham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/County_Durham "County Durham")[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-3) and attended [Richmond School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richmond_School "Richmond School"), [North Yorkshire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North_Yorkshire "North Yorkshire").

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Television work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Television work")]

Farnaby was a long-time member of _[The Mighty Boosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mighty\_Boosh "The Mighty Boosh")_ supporting cast,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-metro-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-ie-5) having had roles both in their series and co-starring in the quasi-spinoff film _[Bunny and the Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunny\_and\_the\_Bull "Bunny and the Bull")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-bunny-6)

Other notable television work includes recurring roles in the sitcoms _[Jam & Jerusalem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jam\_&\_Jerusalem "Jam & Jerusalem")_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)_[The Midnight Beast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Midnight\_Beast\_(TV\_series) "The Midnight Beast (TV series)")_[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-metro-4) and _[Detectorists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Detectorists "Detectorists")_. He previously had a very brief role in one episode of _[Coronation Street](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronation\_Street "Coronation Street")_ in the 1990s.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)

Farnaby has presented a number of factual programmes including _Richard III: The King in the Car Park_ in 2013,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-8) tracing the [discovery and identification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhumation_of_Richard_III_of_England "Exhumation of Richard III of England") of the remains of the last [Plantagenet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plantagenet "Plantagenet") king, the 2014 Channel 4 documentary series entitled _Man Vs Weird_, in which he travelled the world investigating people who claim superhuman abilities,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-9) and as narrator of the [Channel 5](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_5_(UK) "Channel 5 (UK)") docu-series called _[On the Yorkshire Buses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/On\_the\_Yorkshire\_Buses "On the Yorkshire Buses")_, following [East Yorkshire Motor Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Yorkshire_Motor_Services "East Yorkshire Motor Services").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-10)

Farnaby accepted a [TV BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") in 2023 for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment"), for a short film broadcast as part of the [Platinum Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Party_at_the_Palace "Platinum Party at the Palace") for the [Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II") of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in June 2022, in which Farnaby played a butler.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2)

#### Them There

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Them There")]

Main article: Them There

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2a/The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg/250px-The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children%27s_BAFTAs%2C_27_November_2011.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_starring_cast_of_TV_series_Horrible_Histories_arrives_at_the_Children's_BAFTAs,_27_November_2011.jpg)

L-R: Simon Farnaby, [Martha Howe-Douglas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas "Martha Howe-Douglas"), Mathew Baynton, [Laurence Rickard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Rickard "Laurence Rickard"), Ben Willbond and Jim Howick at the 2011 Children's [BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTAs "BAFTAs").

Farnaby has worked extensively with the Them There collective of six writers and actors, who started as principal members of the cast of the [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC") live-action series _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, where he played offbeat characters including [Caligula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caligula "Caligula") and Death.

Farnaby, along with the five other collective members, co-created, wrote and starred in _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_ (2013–2016),[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-11) which was broadcast on [Sky One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sky_One "Sky One") for three series.

Farnaby had his first major involvement with the creation of a film with the troupe, on the 2015 historical comedy film _[Bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill\_(2015\_film) "Bill (2015 film)")_, based loosely around the early life of [William Shakespeare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Shakespeare "William Shakespeare").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-13)

The same collective then went on to create the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") show _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_, which ran for five seasons before the team decided to retire it.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-14) Farnaby played the fictitious [Conservative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK) "Conservative Party (UK)") politician ghost, Julian Fawcett,[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-15) who always appeared without trousers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-mylondon-7)

### Books

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Books")]

Along with journalist Scott Murray, in 2011 Farnaby co-wrote _[The Phantom of the Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Open "The Phantom of the Open")_, a biography of [Maurice Flitcroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Flitcroft "Maurice Flitcroft"), a would-be professional golfer whose unsuccessful attempts to qualify for the [Open Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Championship "Open Championship") led to his being described as "the world's worst golfer".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-chortle-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-17)

His first children's novel, _The Wizard In My Shed_, was published in 2020,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-18) and this was followed by a sequel titled _Warrior in my Wardrobe: More Misadventures with Merdyn the Wild_, which was released in 2021.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-20)

Farnaby was also a co-author of _Ghosts: The Button House Archives_, a companion book to the Them There television series for the BBC, _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_British\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 British TV series)")_ which he co-wrote and starred in.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-22)

### Films

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Simon_Farnaby&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Films")]

Having previously appeared in _[The Mighty Boosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mighty\_Boosh "The Mighty Boosh")_, Farnaby was in a starring role for the related film _[Bunny and the Bull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bunny\_and\_the\_Bull "Bunny and the Bull")_ in 2009, where he played the eponymous Bunny.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-bunny-6)

In 2016, Farnaby co-wrote and had a small acting part in _[Mindhorn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindhorn "Mindhorn")_ with [Julian Barratt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julian_Barratt "Julian Barratt"), a comedy about Richard Thorncroft (Barratt), a faded television actor drawn into negotiations with a criminal who believes his character Detective Mindhorn is real.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-ie-5)

He co-wrote the book _The Phantom of the Open_ about golfer [Maurice Flitcroft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maurice_Flitcroft "Maurice Flitcroft") in 2011, and then started work on a film script of the story in 2017, which led to the release of _[The Phantom of the Open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Phantom\_of\_the\_Open "The Phantom of the Open")_ in 2021, starring [Mark Rylance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mark_Rylance "Mark Rylance").

Also in 2016, Farnaby had a small on-screen role in _[Rogue One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rogue\_One "Rogue One")_, as an X-Wing pilot.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-23)

The biggest film success of Farnaby's career came with the [Paddington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington_(film) "Paddington (film)") film franchise. Following on from appearing as an actor in [the first film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington_(film) "Paddington (film)"), he went on to co-write _[Paddington 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington\_2 "Paddington 2")_ with [Paul King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_King_(director) "Paul King (director)"), for which he was nominated for two [film BAFTAs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Film_Awards "British Academy Film Awards") for [best adapted screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Best_Adapted_Screenplay "BAFTA Award for Best Adapted Screenplay") and [Outstanding British Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BAFTA_Award_for_Outstanding_British_Film "BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film"). He was also the winner of the International Online Cinema Award for Best Adapted Screenplay, and the [Hollywood Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Critics_Association "Hollywood Critics Association") award for Best Adapted Screenplay in 2018.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-24) Farnaby subsequently appeared alongside [Paddington Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddington_Bear "Paddington Bear") and [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in a short film broadcast as a part of the [Platinum Party at the Palace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Party_at_the_Palace "Platinum Party at the Palace") for the [Platinum Jubilee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platinum_Jubilee_of_Elizabeth_II "Platinum Jubilee of Elizabeth II") of [Queen Elizabeth II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_II "Queen Elizabeth II") in June 2022, which won the 2023 [BAFTA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Awards "British Academy Television Awards") for [memorable TV moment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Academy_Television_Award_for_P&O_Cruises_Memorable_Moment "British Academy Television Award for P&O Cruises Memorable Moment"), which Farnaby accepted.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-tvbafta-2)

Farnaby is the co-writer of 2023 Christmas release _[Wonka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonka\_(film) "Wonka (film)")_, along with [Paul King](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_King_(director) "Paul King (director)"), which is a prequel to _[Charlie and the Chocolate Factory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlie\_and\_the\_Chocolate\_Factory "Charlie and the Chocolate Factory")_ by [Roald Dahl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roald_Dahl "Roald Dahl").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-25) Alongside _Ghosts_ co-star [Charlotte Ritchie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte_Ritchie "Charlotte Ritchie"), Farnaby also has a small on-screen role, with his Them There collaborator Mathew Baynton in one of the leading roles, and starring [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timoth%C3%A9e_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet").

Farnaby wrote the screenplay for [The Magic Faraway Tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Magic_Faraway_Tree_(film) "The Magic Faraway Tree (film)").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-26) An adaptation of [Enid Blyton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enid_Blyton "Enid Blyton")'s book series of the [same name](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Faraway_Tree "The Faraway Tree"). The film released theatrically in the UK on 27 March 2026.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Farnaby#cite_note-27)

## Personal life

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the Them There collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Martha_Howe-Douglas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Martha_Howe-Douglas&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Martha_Howe-Douglas&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

**Martha Howe-Douglas** (born 1981 or 1982) is an English actress and writer. She is known as a member of the Them There collective with which she wrote and starred in productions including _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_, _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, and _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_. She also played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") daytime soap _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-1)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Martha_Howe-Douglas&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Howe-Douglas was born and raised in [Moseley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moseley "Moseley"), a suburb of south [Birmingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birmingham "Birmingham"), [England](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/England "England"), in 1981 or 1982.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2) She attended Edgbaston High School.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-3) She graduated from [RADA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RADA "RADA") in 2003.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-ashbee.net-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Martha_Howe-Douglas&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

After graduating from RADA, Howe-Douglas appeared in the Christmas special of _[The Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Office\_(UK\_TV\_series) "The Office (UK TV series)")_, as a receptionist at Wernham-Hogg.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-6) From 24 April 2006 until 11 May 2007, Howe-Douglas played receptionist [Donna Parmar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Parmar "Donna Parmar") in the [BBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC "BBC") daytime soap opera _[Doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctors\_(2000\_TV\_series) "Doctors (2000 TV series)")_. For her role as Donna, Howe-Douglas received nominations for [Best Comedy Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Comedy_Performance "British Soap Award for Best Comedy Performance") and [Best Newcomer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Soap_Award_for_Best_Newcomer "British Soap Award for Best Newcomer") at the [2007 British Soap Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007_British_Soap_Awards "2007 British Soap Awards").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-2007_BSAs-7)

In 2009, she landed one of the main multi-role parts on a new children's TV history sketch show programme, [CBBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBBC "CBBC")'s _[Horrible Histories](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horrible\_Histories\_(2009\_TV\_series) "Horrible Histories (2009 TV series)")_,[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-8) where over five years and five series, she played numerous characters including the queens [Cleopatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cleopatra "Cleopatra"), [Elizabeth I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_I "Elizabeth I"), [Boudicea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boudicea "Boudicea") and [Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria"). In 2011, she appeared in _[The Proms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Proms "The Proms")_, in a special live "_Horrible Histories_ Big Prom Party" performance.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-9) In 2013, she co-created, co-wrote and co-starred in Sky1's series _[Yonderland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yonderland "Yonderland")_, in which she played lead character Debbie Maddox[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-10) in all three series.

Howe-Douglas' other acting roles have included appearing in _[The Armstrong & Miller Show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Armstrong\_&\_Miller\_Show "The Armstrong & Miller Show")_ on [BBC One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BBC_One "BBC One") and playing Flora Dies-Early in the radio comedy show _[Bleak Expectations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bleak\_Expectations "Bleak Expectations")_, as well as Lady Anne Woodstock in the radio show _[The Castle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Castle\_(radio\_series) "The Castle (radio series)")_. In 2018, she appeared in the BBC soap opera _[EastEnders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EastEnders "EastEnders")_ as [Annie Pritchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_EastEnders_characters_introduced_in_2018#Annie_Pritchard "List of EastEnders characters introduced in 2018").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-11) From 15 April 2019, Howe-Douglas co-wrote, produced and starred in the BBC sitcom _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_, which sees her reunited with the _Horrible Histories_ cast.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-12)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Martha_Howe-Douglas&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Howe-Douglas is married to a photographer who worked on _[Ghosts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghosts\_(2019\_TV\_series) "Ghosts (2019 TV series)")_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martha_Howe-Douglas#cite_note-13)

The **91st Academy Awards** ceremony, presented by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") (AMPAS), honored the best [films of 2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018_in_film "2018 in film") and took place on February 24, 2019, at the [Dolby Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolby_Theatre "Dolby Theatre") in [Hollywood, Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood,_Los_Angeles "Hollywood, Los Angeles"). During the ceremony, AMPAS presented [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") (commonly referred to as Oscars) in 24 categories. The ceremony was televised in the United States by the [American Broadcasting Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") (ABC) and was produced by [Donna Gigliotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Gigliotti "Donna Gigliotti") and [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss"), with Weiss also serving as director.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-THROscarProducers-2) This was the first telecast to have no host since the [61st ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/61st_Academy_Awards "61st Academy Awards") held in 1989.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-nohost-6)

In related events, the Academy held its 10th Annual [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards") ceremony at the Grand Ballroom of the [Hollywood & Highland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_&_Highland "Hollywood & Highland") Center on November 18, 2018.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Governors-7) The [Academy Scientific and Technical Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Scientific_and_Technical_Award "Academy Scientific and Technical Award") were presented by host [David Oyelowo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Oyelowo "David Oyelowo") on February 9, 2019, in a ceremony at the [Beverly Wilshire Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Wilshire_Hotel "Beverly Wilshire Hotel") in [Beverly Hills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills "Beverly Hills").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-8)

_[Green Book](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green\_Book\_(film) "Green Book (film)")_ won three awards, including [Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-10)_[Bohemian Rhapsody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bohemian\_Rhapsody\_(film) "Bohemian Rhapsody (film)")_ won the most awards of the night, with four awards. _[Black Panther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Panther\_(film) "Black Panther (film)")_ and _[Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roma\_(2018\_film) "Roma (2018 film)")_ won three awards, and _[Bao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bao\_(film) "Bao (film)")_, _[BlacKkKlansman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BlacKkKlansman "BlacKkKlansman")_, _[The Favourite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Favourite\_(2018\_film) "The Favourite (2018 film)")_, _[First Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First\_Man\_(film) "First Man (film)")_, _[Free Solo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free\_Solo "Free Solo")_, _[If Beale Street Could Talk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/If\_Beale\_Street\_Could\_Talk\_(film) "If Beale Street Could Talk (film)")_, _[Period. End of Sentence.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Period.\_End\_of\_Sentence. "Period. End of Sentence.")_, _[Skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin\_(2018\_short\_film) "Skin (2018 short film)")_, _[Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider-Man:\_Into\_the\_Spider-Verse "Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse")_, _[A Star Is Born](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Star\_Is\_Born\_(2018\_film) "A Star Is Born (2018 film)")_, and _[Vice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice\_(2018\_film) "Vice (2018 film)")_ each won one. The telecast garnered 29.56 million viewers in the United States.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-ABCNielsen-4)

The nominees for the 91st Academy Awards were announced on January 22, 2019, at 5:20 a.m. PST (13:20 [UTC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC "UTC")), at the Academy headquarters in Beverly Hills, by actors [Kumail Nanjiani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kumail_Nanjiani "Kumail Nanjiani") and [Tracee Ellis Ross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracee_Ellis_Ross "Tracee Ellis Ross").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-WapoOscars-11)_[The Favourite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Favourite\_(2018\_film) "The Favourite (2018 film)")_ and _[Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roma\_(2018\_film) "Roma (2018 film)")_ tied for the most nominations with ten each.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-12)

The winners were announced during the awards ceremony on February 24, 2019.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-13) For the second time since the expansion of the Best Picture nominee roster at the [82nd ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Academy_Awards "82nd Academy Awards") in 2010, every Best Picture nominee won at least one award.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-14)_[Roma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roma\_(2018\_film) "Roma (2018 film)")_ became the fifth film nominated simultaneously for Best Picture and Best Foreign Language Film in the same year.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-15)[Alfonso Cuarón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_Cuar%C3%B3n "Alfonso Cuarón") was the first person to win Best Director and Best Cinematography for the same film.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-16)_[Black Panther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_Panther\_(film) "Black Panther (film)")_ was the first [superhero film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superhero_film "Superhero film") to be nominated for Best Picture.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-17)

Best Actress nominee [Yalitza Aparicio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yalitza_Aparicio "Yalitza Aparicio") was the first Indigenous Mexican person nominated for an acting Oscar.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-18) Best Supporting Actor winner [Mahershala Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahershala_Ali "Mahershala Ali") became the [second black performer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_black_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees "List of black Academy Award winners and nominees") to win multiple acting awards after [Denzel Washington](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denzel_Washington "Denzel Washington"), who won Best Supporting Actor for 1989's _[Glory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glory\_(1989\_film) "Glory (1989 film)")_ and Best Actor for 2001's _[Training Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Training\_Day "Training Day")_.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-19) With her nomination for Best Actress and win for Best Original Song for co-writing "[Shallow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shallow_(Lady_Gaga_and_Bradley_Cooper_song) "Shallow (Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper song)")" from _[A Star Is Born](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Star\_Is\_Born\_(2018\_film) "A Star Is Born (2018 film)")_, [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga") was the second person to receive acting and songwriting nominations for the same film, after [Mary J. Blige](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_J._Blige "Mary J. Blige") for 2017's _[Mudbound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mudbound\_(film) "Mudbound (film)")_, and the first person to do so in a leading role and win in either or both categories.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-20)[Hannah Beachler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hannah_Beachler "Hannah Beachler") became the first [black Best Production Design nominee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_black_Academy_Award_winners_and_nominees#Best_Production_Design "List of black Academy Award winners and nominees").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-21) Both her and Best Costume Design winner [Ruth E. Carter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruth_E._Carter "Ruth E. Carter") were the first black winners in their respective categories,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-22) as well as the first black women to win in a non-acting category since [Irene Cara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irene_Cara "Irene Cara"), who won the category of Best Original Song for co-writing "[Flashdance... What a Feeling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashdance..._What_a_Feeling "Flashdance... What a Feeling")" from 1983's _[Flashdance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flashdance "Flashdance")_.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-23)

### Governors Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=91st_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Governors Awards")]

The Academy held its 10th annual [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards") ceremony on November 18, 2018, where the following awards were presented:[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Governors-7)

#### Honorary Awards

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=91st_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Honorary Awards")]

*   To [Marvin Levy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvin_Levy_(publicist) "Marvin Levy (publicist)"), for an exemplary career in publicity that has brought films to the minds, hearts and souls of audiences all over the world.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-HonoraryandSpecial-25)
*   To [Lalo Schifrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lalo_Schifrin "Lalo Schifrin"), in recognition of his unique musical style, compositional integrity and influential contributions to the art of film scoring.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-HonoraryandSpecial-25)
*   To [Cicely Tyson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicely_Tyson "Cicely Tyson"), whose unforgettable performances and personal integrity have inspired generations of filmmakers, actors and audiences.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-HonoraryandSpecial-25)

#### Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=91st_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award")]

The award honors "creative producers whose bodies of work reflect a consistently high quality of motion picture production".[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-26)

*   [Kathleen Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathleen_Kennedy_(producer) "Kathleen Kennedy (producer)") and [Frank Marshall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Marshall_(filmmaker) "Frank Marshall (filmmaker)").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Thalberg-27)

## Ceremony information

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=91st_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Ceremony information")]

On October 22, 2018, the Academy hired film producer [Donna Gigliotti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donna_Gigliotti "Donna Gigliotti") and television producer [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") to oversee production of the 2019 ceremony. "Donna and Glenn will infuse new energy and vision into this 91st awards presentation, and we are excited about a broad-based creative relationship with these two artists", Academy President [John Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bailey_(cinematographer) "John Bailey (cinematographer)") said in a press release announcing the decision. Furthermore, AMPAS CEO [Dawn Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dawn_Hudson "Dawn Hudson") added, "We're thrilled to work with someone as passionate about the Academy as Donna Gigliotti — an Oscar winner and multiple nominee. She and the now-famous Glenn Weiss are committed to making the most of the innovations we've embraced for our 91st Oscars."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-THROscarProducers-2)

On December 4, 2018, _[Deadline Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadline\_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ reported that actor and comedian [Kevin Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hart "Kevin Hart") was considered as the host by the Academy and ABC.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-31) On the same day he announced via [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram") that he would host the show.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-32) Afterwards, social media used reminded about anti-gay slurs and language is his old [tweets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tweet_(social_media) "Tweet (social media)") and stand-up routines nearly a decade ago. In a response, the Academy warned him that if he wouldn't apologize, he would be dismissed. On December 6, 2018, he announced that he resigned from hosting, arguing that he had already apologized multiple times and adding: "I'm not going to continue to go back and tap into the days of old when I've moved on and I'm in a completely different place in my life." He also added he did not want to be a "distraction" to the ceremony in light of the controversy.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-34) The following February, broadcaster [ABC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Broadcasting_Company "American Broadcasting Company") Entertainment chief Karey Burke announced that the festivities would proceed without a host.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-nohost-6) During an interview at the [Television Critics Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Television_Critics_Association "Television Critics Association") press tour, Burke stated, "The main goal, which I was told, was the Academy promised ABC last year after a very lengthy telecast to keep the show to three hours. Producers wisely decided not to have a host and to go back to having the presenters and movies be the stars, and that be the best way to keep the show at a brisk three hours."[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-35)

Other people participated in the production of the ceremony. Production designer [David Korins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Korins "David Korins") designed a new stage for the show, featuring 41,000 [Swarovski](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swarovski "Swarovski") crystals, thousands of Swarovski beads and pearls, as well as roses.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-36) Randy Thomas served as announcer for the ceremony.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-37) Musician [Rickey Minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rickey_Minor "Rickey Minor") was hired as music director and conductor.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-38)[Queen + Adam Lambert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_+_Adam_Lambert "Queen + Adam Lambert") performed a medley of the songs "[We Will Rock You](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Will_Rock_You "We Will Rock You")" and "[We Are the Champions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/We_Are_the_Champions "We Are the Champions")" as part of the program's opening number.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-39)

### Proposed "Popular Film" category

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=91st_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Proposed \"Popular Film\" category")]

Due to the declining viewership of the recent Academy Awards ceremonies, AMPAS sought new ideas to revamp the show while renewing interest with the nominated films. In August 2018, the organization announced plans to add a new category honoring achievement in "[Popular Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Popular_Film "Academy Award for Outstanding Achievement in Popular Film")".[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-40) The proposal was met with criticism because the award's implied focus on [blockbuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)") suggested that [artistic films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Art_film "Art film") and other non-mainstream pictures were not "popular with audiences".[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-WaPoPopular_Oscars-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-43) Furthermore, many viewed the creation of this new category to be a ploy to boost ratings and that it could hamper critically successful mainstream films from being nominated for Best Picture despite the insistence of AMPAS that such movies could be eligible for both categories.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-WaPoPopular_Oscars-41)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-44) In light of the backlash, the Academy announced the following month that it would postpone implementation of the new category in order to seek additional input.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-45) AMPAS president [John Bailey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Bailey_(cinematographer) "John Bailey (cinematographer)") later admitted that the proposed category was intended to help improve viewership, and noted that the concept of a separate award for commercial film dates back to the [inaugural awards ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1st_Academy_Awards "1st Academy Awards"), which had separate categories for "Outstanding Picture" and "Best Unique and Artistic Picture".[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-46)

### Unsuccessful efforts to shorten the ceremony

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=91st_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Unsuccessful efforts to shorten the ceremony")]

In an effort to shorten the ceremony, it was reported that only two of the nominees for [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Academy Award for Best Original Song"), "[All the Stars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_the_Stars "All the Stars")" and "[Shallow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shallow_(Lady_Gaga_and_Bradley_Cooper_song) "Shallow (Lady Gaga and Bradley Cooper song)")", would be performed live.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-47) According to [Diane Warren](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diane_Warren "Diane Warren"), [Lady Gaga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lady_Gaga "Lady Gaga") decided not to perform if the other three songs would be excluded.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-48) After a negative reaction from audiences and industry musicians, including [Lin-Manuel Miranda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lin-Manuel_Miranda "Lin-Manuel Miranda") and members of the music branch, the Academy backtracked and announced that all five Best Original Song nominees would be performed during the ceremony.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-50) "All the Stars" would not be performed, however, with _Variety_ reporting that there were "logistics and timing issues" with its performers, [Kendrick Lamar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendrick_Lamar "Kendrick Lamar") and [SZA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SZA "SZA").[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-51)

On February 11, AMPAS announced that the presentation of four awards categories, [Best Cinematography](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Cinematography "Academy Award for Best Cinematography"), [Best Live Action Short Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Best_Live_Action_Short_Film "Best Live Action Short Film"), [Best Film Editing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Film_Editing "Academy Award for Best Film Editing"), and [Best Makeup and Hairstyling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Makeup_and_Hairstyling "Academy Award for Best Makeup and Hairstyling"), would occur during commercial breaks.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-52) They said that these presentations would be streamed so viewers could watch them live online, and that the winners' acceptance speeches would be replayed later in the broadcast.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-53) The decision received extensive backlash from audiences. Several filmmakers, including [Guillermo del Toro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guillermo_del_Toro "Guillermo del Toro"), [Christopher Nolan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Nolan "Christopher Nolan"), [Martin Scorsese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_Scorsese "Martin Scorsese"), [Quentin Tarantino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quentin_Tarantino "Quentin Tarantino"), [Damien Chazelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damien_Chazelle "Damien Chazelle"), [Spike Lee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spike_Lee "Spike Lee"), [Joe Dante](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Dante "Joe Dante") and [Alfonso Cuarón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfonso_Cuar%C3%B3n "Alfonso Cuarón") (the latter of whom was nominated and won in one of the aforementioned categories), signed on to an open letter to the Academy asking it to reverse its decision.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-54) Four days later, the Academy reversed the decision and announced that all 24 categories would be presented live.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-All_Oscar_Categories_to_Air_Live_After_Hollywood_Protest-55)

### Box office performance of Best Picture nominees

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=91st_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Box office performance of Best Picture nominees")]

When the nominations were announced, seven of the eight films nominated for Best Picture had earned a combined gross of $1.26 billion at the American and Canadian box offices at the time.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Variety2019BoxOfficeOscars-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-57)_Black Panther_ was the highest-grossing film among the Best Picture nominees with $700 million in domestic box office receipts. _A Star is Born_ came in second with $204.8 million; this was followed by _Bohemian Rhapsody_ ($202.4 million), _BlacKkKlansman_ ($48.5 million), _Green Book_ ($42.3 million), _Vice_ ($39.5 million), and _The Favourite_ ($23 million).[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-58) Box office figures for _Roma_ were unavailable due to distributor [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s policy of refusing to release such figures.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-Variety2019BoxOfficeOscars-56)

### Critical reviews and ratings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=91st_Academy_Awards&action=edit&section=14 "Edit section: Critical reviews and ratings")]

Some media outlets received the broadcast positively. Chuck Barney of _[The Mercury News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Mercury\_News "The Mercury News")_ commented, "After months of bad buzz and embarrassing missteps, the 91st Academy Awards appeared to be on their way to an epic fail." He also remarked, "The show, as usual, had some rocky moments, but overall it was a lively, well-paced and entertaining affair."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-59) Television critic Matthew Gilbert of _[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Boston\_Globe "The Boston Globe")_ wrote, "The hostless Oscar ceremony felt a little more streamlined and energetic than usual, as we were spared yet another predictable opening goof on the nominated movies, a monologue pretending to make fun of the stars, and short quips across the night that never quite land."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-60)_[The Hollywood Reporter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hollywood\_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")_ television critic Daniel Fienberg quipped, "Sunday's Oscars telecast definitely confirmed that under the right circumstances, a host isn't a necessity." In addition, he said, "The show was not overwhelmed by montages or stunts or tributes, and it also wasn't weighed down by elaborately prepared presenter schtick."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-61)

Others were more critical of the show. Kelly Lawler of _[USA Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/USA\_Today "USA Today")_ wrote, "The 2019 Oscar telecast lacked energy and comedy, and was treacherously dull. And maybe that could have been avoided if the Academy had done what it has (almost) always done, and procured a host." She also observed that the awards "were more like a press conference with movie clips in the middle".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#cite_note-62) Television critic [Hank Stuever](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Stuever "Hank Stuever") of _[The Washington Post](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Washington\_Post "The Washington Post")_ commented, "They kept all the speeches but lost any trace of the unpredictable magic.
